name: io.github.ArpitGandhi1934/yugenox-jobs
title: Yugenox Jobs: Search Open Jobs, Match a Resume, See Who's Hiring
description: Open jobs from employers' own postings, mostly US/Canada, updated daily. 20 free searches a month.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search open job postings from thousands of employers (no agencies), US, Canada and more, updated daily. Use title for job titles (every word must be in the title: the precise way to match roles or a resume) and query for skills or keywords anywhere in a posting. Returns up to 10 postings per call: title, company, location, pay when posted, posted date, days open, a link to the posting on Yugenox Jobs and the employer's apply link. Page with offset (first 100 results). Call get_job for the full description.

query.description: Keywords anywhere in a posting (title, team or description), e.g. "power bi", "kubernetes", "registered nurse". Postings with every keyword in the title come first. For job titles use title.

title.description: Words that must all be in the job title, e.g. "data analytics manager", "registered nurse". The precise way to match roles or a resume: one call per likely title. Supports "exact phrase", or, and -word.

location.description: Where: a city with its state or province code ("Toronto, ON", "Austin, TX": exact and fastest), a province, state or country ("Ontario", "Texas", "Canada"), "Remote, Canada" for remote jobs open to that country, or "Remote" for remote jobs in any country.

company.description: Employer name, e.g. "Stripe". A close spelling ("Stripe Inc", "Acme Software") finds the employer and says which one it used.

remote.description: true = remote jobs only (with location set to a country: remote jobs open to that country); false = no remote jobs.

min_salary.description: Yearly pay floor (hourly pay counts as yearly). Only postings that publish pay match. Currency: the place searched (CAD for Canada, USD for the US) unless currency is set.

currency.description: Three-letter currency for min_salary, e.g. USD, CAD, GBP.

posted_within_days.description: Only postings published in the last N days: by the employer's own posting date, or, for employers that publish none, the day the posting first appeared in the index. Undated postings that were already listed when an employer was first indexed in full, and undated postings of employers not yet indexed in full, have no known date and are left out.

sort.description: relevance (the default when query is set) or newest.

offset.description: Skip this many results (next_offset from the previous call).

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: One posting in full: description, pay, locations, dates, whether it is still open (or unconfirmed: its employer's job site could not be re-checked lately), the company's open-role count and the employer's apply link. For some postings the description is loaded from the employer's page on request (a few seconds). Pass the id from search_jobs (or a Yugenox Jobs /job/... link).

job_id.description: The id field of a search_jobs result, or a Yugenox Jobs job link (/job/...).

tools.name: match_resume
tools.description: Rank open job postings by how well their words match a resume: job title and level, skills, and years of experience. Pass the resume as plain text; titles (comma-separated) picks the roles to search, otherwise the resume's recent titles are used. Returns up to 10 postings, each with a 0-100 match score, the skills it names that the resume has and lacks, and the years it asks for. A word match, not a hiring prediction. The resume is used only for this call: never stored or logged.

resume.description: The resume as plain text (up to 30,000 characters). Used only for this call: never stored, logged or returned.

titles.description: Target job titles, comma-separated, e.g. "data analyst, business intelligence analyst" (the first 3 are searched). Left out: the most recent titles on the resume.

location.description: Where: a city with its state or province code ("Toronto, ON", "Austin, TX"), a province, state or country, or "Remote". Left out: the city on the resume, if it names one.

remote.description: true = remote jobs only; false = no remote jobs.

posted_within_days.description: Only postings published in the last N days (the same rule as search_jobs: the employer's own date, else the day the posting first appeared in the index).

tools.name: company_hiring
tools.description: How one employer is hiring: open postings and distinct roles, the change over 7 days, roles opened and closed in the last 30 days by team and city, top departments and countries, and its newest roles with links. Pass a company name (or a careers / job board link). If several companies match, it lists them: call again with the exact name.

company.description: Company name, e.g. "Stripe", or its careers page / job board link.

tools.name: top_hiring_companies
tools.description: Which employers have the most open roles for a job title, role family and/or place, e.g. "data engineer" in "Toronto". Ranks companies by distinct open roles among the newest 3,000 matching postings; each row links to that company's matching jobs. Give at least one of title, role or location.

title.description: Words in the job title, e.g. "data engineer", "nurse", "account executive".

role.description: A role family, when no exact title is wanted.

location.description: A city, state or province, or country: "Toronto", "Texas", "Canada". "Remote" = remote jobs.

posted_within_days.description: Only postings published in the last N days.

tools.name: salary_range
tools.description: The pay employers post for a job title on open postings: its median, middle half and 10th to 90th percentiles, employers ranked by it, and example postings. Give title (every word must be in the job title, as in search_jobs) and optionally location ("Toronto, ON", a province, state or country), remote, query (skills). Amounts are in the place's currency (CAD for Canada, USD for the US) unless currency is set; mostly hourly roles are shown per hour; day, week or month pay counts per year. Only postings that publish pay count, and the answer says how many. For one posting's pay, use get_job.

title.description: Words that must all be in the job title, e.g. "data analytics manager", "registered nurse". The precise way to match roles or a resume: one call per likely title. Supports "exact phrase", or, and -word.

query.description: Skills or keywords anywhere in a posting (title, team or description), e.g. "power bi", "sql": only postings that have them count. For job titles use title.

location.description: Where: a city with its state or province code ("Toronto, ON", "Austin, TX": exact and fastest), a province, state or country ("Ontario", "Texas", "Canada"), "Remote, Canada" for remote jobs open to that country, or "Remote" for remote jobs in any country.

remote.description: true = remote jobs only (with location set to a country: remote jobs open to that country); false = no remote jobs.

posted_within_days.description: Only postings published in the last N days: by the employer's own posting date, or, for employers that publish none, the day the posting first appeared in the index. Undated postings that were already listed when an employer was first indexed in full, and undated postings of employers not yet indexed in full, have no known date and are left out.

currency.description: Three-letter currency of the amounts, e.g. USD, CAD, GBP: only pay posted in it counts. Left out: the place's currency (CAD for Canada, USD for the US); with no place, or a place whose currency is not known, the currency most matching postings use.
